title: Proper direct image on the localizing categories
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible and $p\colon X\to Y$ proper. Suppose that $Rp_*$ maps $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into
$\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ and preserves direct sums of objects of $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. Then $Rp_*$ restricts to an
exact, sum-preserving functor $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$. The hypotheses hold:

- for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$, by [sk-thm-sfb-proper-base-change] and [sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window-ii] (sums in
  $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\subset\Dic(X,\Lambda)$);
- for $\Lambda=A$ finite, by [sk-prop-ctf-finite-proper];
- for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, by [sk-prop-int-compactness], using $\Dctf=\Dbc$.

proof.text:
$Rp_*$ is exact on $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. The argument of [det-proper-image-localizing-principle]
applies with "preserves direct sums" required only for families in $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$: the
subcategory $\mathcal S=\{K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda)):Rp_*K\in\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))\}$ contains $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$,
is triangulated, and for a family $(K_s)$ in $\mathcal S$, $Rp_*\bigoplus K_s\cong\bigoplus Rp_*K_s\in\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$.
So $\mathcal S$ is localizing and equals $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.

For $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$: $\Dctf=\Dbc$, $Rp_*$ preserves $\Dbc$ by [sk-thm-sfb-proper-base-change], and since
$\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))\subset\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ ([sk-cor-ambient-ind-derived]),
[sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window-ii] gives preservation of sums. The other cases are quoted.
